messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Error rate > 8% over the last 5m, p50 latency spiked. Paging oncall-maria :rotating_light:
oncall-maria: Got the page, looking. First call: is prod affected for all customers or a subset?
zach: visible errors are concentrated on scheduling/batching path. Gateway returning 504 and some 502s. Adding logs now.
alex: I see batching scheduler queue depth jumping on several nodes (gw-batch-*-usw2). Head-of-line blocking; some batches taking 30s to assemble then timing out.
eng-runtime: Copy. Oncall-maria — can you run quick health checks and dump queue lengths?
oncall-maria: Running:
```
# curl control plane
curl -s http://batching-usw2.internal/metrics | grep queue_length
queue_length{node="gw-batch-01"} 152
queue_length{node="gw-batch-02"} 148
queue_length{node="gw-batch-03"} 12
```
Looks like two nodes saturated. Why is gw-batch-03 fine?
zach: gw-batch-03 is on different rack (noisy-neighbor avoided), others on the same hostpool that recently had a canary deploy of kernel runtime 1.4.2.
alex: Can we A/B route traffic away from the saturated pool? If we reroute by policy to alternate pool that should reduce head-of-line.
eng-runtime: We have an automated fallback but it hasn't kicked in because model-variant affinity prevented it. Quick fix: relax affinity for 10m to allow fallthrough. I'll apply.
eng-runtime: Pushing config change: `routing.fallback.relax_affinity=true` (applied to us-west-2)
deploy-bot: config change queued, deploying to control-plane (rollout-id: r-20250318-003)
oncall-maria: After change: queue lengths:
```
queue_length{node="gw-batch-01"} 98
queue_length{node="gw-batch-02"} 87
queue_length{node="gw-batch-03"} 45
```
Errors still present but down from 8% -> 3.4% over last 5m.
customer-success: Any known customer impact? We're getting a ticket from Acme with timeouts — do we need to proactively reach out?
zach: Impact: started ~10:03 UTC, affects generation requests > 512 tokens and chat flows that hit long sequence lengths. Embeddings unaffected. Some customers see intermittent 504s.
oncall-maria: I'm going to scale up batch workers on gw-batch-01/02 by +2 replicas each as another mitigation.
eng-runtime: Scaling replicas now via autoscaler: set min=4 -> 6 for pool gw-batch-usw2
deploy-bot: scaler change executed (scale-op: s-20250318-007)
oncall-maria: Replica scale applied. Observability shows CPU on those nodes spiked but throughput improving.
alex: Propose we enable prefix KV cache eviction hygiene — old KV entries are causing batch assembly delays for long-chat requests. If we clear some stale KV partitions it'll free the KV cache and speed up dispatch.
eng-runtime: Good call. Preparing KV partition evict for affected hostpool. Doing safe-evict with 30s drain.
eng-runtime: Eviction command:
```
adminctl evict-kv --pool gw-batch-usw2 --partitions 12-15 --grace 30s
```
oncall-maria: Eviction completed. Post-evict metrics:
```
queue_length{node="gw-batch-01"} 21
queue_length{node="gw-batch-02"} 17
errors_5xx_rate 0.8%
p50_latency 220ms
```
zach: Major improvement. Looks like the head-of-line caused by a few long-running batches + stale KV entries. Root cause hypothesis: kernel runtime 1.4.2 changed KV eviction heuristics; combined with recent traffic shift it caused batch buildup on specific hosts.
sre-manager: Good mitigation. What's next for root cause and postmortem owners?
alex: Next steps: roll back the kernel canary on that hostpool, run a targeted diff on eviction heuristics, and schedule a regression test in staging for long-sequence workloads. I can own rollback + regression.
eng-runtime: I'll collect heap/KV metrics and kernel logs from gw-batch-01/02 and attach to incident. Also will draft a hotfix for KV eviction sensitivity.
customer-success: I'll notify the affected customers (Acme, BetaCorp) with a summary and ETA for follow-up. No SLA breach expected but will offer post-incident review.
oncall-maria: Current status: traffic stabilized, errors <1% and latency normalizing. I'm leaving monitoring on for 2h and handing off to alex for follow-up. Paging cleared.
alex: Taking follow-up. I will open the postmortem and actionable items: rollback canary, add canary test for KV eviction, make fallback routing less strict, and improve alerting to detect head-of-line cluster-local saturation earlier.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: status changed -> mitigated. Incident lead: alex. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring. Channel: #incidents. Logs archived (run id: inc-20250318-173500)
sre-manager: Thanks team. Leave the thread open for updates and make sure all action items have owners in the postmortem.
oncall-maria: Closing my oncall shift notes here: immediate mitigations performed: relaxed affinity, scaled replicas, KV eviction. No customer-facing downtime reported beyond transient 504s. Handed to alex.
alex: I'll create the postmortem doc and link the logs. Will tag eng-runtime and observability for metric dashboards. Expected write-up by EOD tomorrow.
